# Redstone-lite feasibility report — monecraft

Facts with `file:line` references. All paths absolute.

## 1. Engine step order & where a "redstone" system slots

**Authoritative source:** `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` `step(dt, input?)` at **`GameEngine.ts:530`**. The doc `docs/architecture.md:44-59` matches it. Verified per-frame order (non-replica, alive, not paused/sleeping):

Pre-loop gates: pause (`:532`), replica early-return (`:549`), local-death freeze (`:577`), sleep freeze (`:593`).

Per-player loop `stepPlayer` (`:600-610`, body at `:630`):
1. Stuck/unstuck (`:646`)
2. Player/vehicle motion (`:664-676`)
3. Hunger/regen/starvation/status/water/lava/oxygen (`:681-703`, all in `systems/playerStats.ts`)
4. **Mining + placement** `tickMining` (`:706`) — block edits happen here
5. Fishing (`:707`)

Then world-level systems (`:612-624`), in order:
- `tickDayNight` (`:612`), `tickWeather` (`:613`)
- `tickRandomBlocks` (`:614`) — `systems/randomTicks.ts`
- spawn directors (`:615-617`)
- `tickMobs` (`:618`) — mob AI + creeper explosions
- **`tickPrimedTnt`** (`:619`) — TNT fuse countdown + detonation
- `tickProjectiles` (`:620`), `tickThrownSpears` (`:621`), `tickBreeding` (`:622`), `tickRaid` (`:623`)
- `tickDebugInfo` (`:624`), then `refreshSnapshot()` (`:626`)

**Systems are plain functions over `GameState`**, invoked positionally in `step`; each receives `(state, dt, …deps)`. There is **no registry/scheduler** — the call order in `step` *is* the schedule (`docs/architecture.md:42`, `adding-content.md:148-150`). Deps like `this.rng`, `this.emit`, `this.surfaceYAt`, `this.mobTickDeps` (`GameEngine.ts:1511`) are passed explicitly.

**Where redstone slots:** A redstone system reads block state and writes block edits, then those edits must be observed by TNT/doors/lamps the same tick. Best placement is **after `tickMining`/placement + interact (which produce lever/button/plate/wire changes) and immediately before `tickPrimedTnt` (`:619`)**, i.e. a new `tickRedstone(state, dt, {rng, emit})` call inserted at ~`:618`. Putting it before `tickPrimedTnt` lets "wire powered → `primeTnt`" ignite on the same tick it counts down. It should run after the per-player loop (so a lever toggled by `dispatch` this frame is visible) — the per-player loop finishes at `:610` before the world systems.

Note: `dispatch` (lever right-click) runs **outside** `step` (event-driven, `GameEngine.ts:720`), mutating state before the next `step`, so redstone reads a consistent snapshot.

## 2. The block-edit chokepoint (`lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts`)

Full file read. `createBlockChangeTracker(world)` returns `set/applySavedChanges/changes/drainEdits/drainEditsDetailed` (`blockChanges.ts:28`).

`set(x,y,z,block)` (`:37-52`) is **the single chokepoint for every gameplay edit**. In order it:
1. bounds-checks (`:38`)
2. records worldgen baseline once per idx (`:40`)
3. `world.set` (`:42`)
4. **`applyEdit(world, world.light, x, y, z)`** — incremental relight (`:47`, from `@/lib/world`)
5. updates the save delta set (drops the cell if restored to baseline) (`:48-50`)
6. appends to the per-tick **`editJournal`** with `{block, prev}` (`:51`)

**Remeshing is NOT in `set`.** Callers set `state.worldMeshDirty = true` themselves after a batch (e.g. `mining.ts:204,265`, `interact.ts:98`, `explosion.ts:101,175`, `randomTicks.ts:30`). The renderer reads/clears it (`GameRenderer.ts:612-614`; minimap `minimap.ts:79`). So a redstone edit must set `worldMeshDirty` once per tick if any block changed.

**Observer vs poll:** There is **no observer/callback** on `set()` — nothing is notified "block changed at idx X." Systems **poll**. The `editJournal` is a *drain* channel, not an event bus: `drainEdits()` (`:71`) / `drainEditsDetailed()` (`:78`) are consumed by the **server room each tick** (`room.ts:439`) and by the replica's prediction ledger (`NetworkSession.ts:509,758`). A redstone system **cannot** use the journal as its change-feed (the server already drains it and it's last-write-wins). Redstone must **poll block state itself** — the precedent is `randomTicks.ts`, which samples columns and dispatches per-block handlers from a `RANDOM_TICK_HANDLERS` map (`adding-content.md:94-99`). A redstone graph would similarly scan/track its own power sources each tick.

`mining.ts` → `set`: break path `mining.ts:178-206` (`blockBroken` emit at `:206`), placement `placeSelectedBlock` `mining.ts:210-267` (doors write two cells `:245-246`; `blockPlaced` emit `:266`). `interact.ts` right-click edits (doors, hoe, seeds, bone-meal) all funnel through `state.blockChanges.set`.

## 3. TNT ignition path

- **Torch → TNT ignite (today):** `tryUseHeldItem` in `interact.ts:291`, branch at `:311-315`: held item id `"torch"` aimed at `BlockId.Tnt` (id 49) calls `primeTnt(state, x, y, z, emit)`. This branch sits in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.ts:934`, chain `:910-935`).
- **`primeTnt`** (`explosion.ts:137-142`): sets `state.primedTnt.set(idx, TNT_FUSE_SECONDS)` (no-op if already lit) and emits `{type:"tntPrimed", x,y,z}`.
- **State structure:** `state.primedTnt: Map<number, number>` — voxelIndex → seconds left on fuse; **session-only, never serialized** (`state.ts:328-329`; save-format confirms `save-format.md:66`). (Creeper fuses are separate: `MobState.fuseTimer`, `state.ts:144-145`.)
- **Explosion entry point:** `tickPrimedTnt(state, dt, deps)` (`explosion.ts:149`) counts down, drops mined/overwritten TNT (`:160-161`), and on expiry clears the cell + calls `explode(...)` (`:173-177`). `explode` (`explosion.ts:58`) destroys blocks via `blockChanges.set` (`:92-95`), chain-primes neighbor TNT (`:79-87`), damages players/mobs, emits `{type:"explosion"}` (`:133`). Ticked at `GameEngine.ts:619`.
- **Where "powered → ignite" hooks:** call the exported **`primeTnt(state, x, y, z, emit)`** from the redstone system when a wire/plate/torch adjacent to a `BlockId.Tnt` cell becomes powered. It's already the shared ignition primitive (`adding-content.md:60-63`). No new explosion plumbing needed.

## 4. Pressure-plate needs ("standing on block X" per-tick precedent)

The precedent is in **`lib/game/engine/systems/playerStats.ts`**, which samples `world.get()` at the player's foot/body/head cell every tick:
- `tickWaterExposure` (`playerStats.ts:122`): `world.get(floor(x), floor(y + PLAYER_HEIGHT*0.5), floor(z))` (`:125-128`)
- `tickLavaExposure` (`:150`): checks **underfoot** `floor(py-0.1)`, feet `floor(py)`, and body `floor(py+PLAYER_HEIGHT*0.5)` (`:162-165`) — the exact "standing on block below feet" pattern a pressure plate wants
- `tickOxygen` (`:192`): head cell `floor(y + EYE_HEIGHT)` (`:207-211`)

These iterate the single primary player; a plate system would loop `state.players.values()` (multiplayer-aware, as `explode` does at `explosion.ts:108`) and, for mobs, `state.mobs`. **There is no cactus-contact or farmland-trample mechanic** — cactus appears only as a footstep material (`audio/materials.ts:30`); no `Cactus` damage code exists in `systems/`. So the water/lava/oxygen exposure checks are the only "standing on block" precedent, and they poll per-tick from within the per-player step (`stepPlayer`, `GameEngine.ts:701-703`). A pressure-plate check would naturally live as a new world-system call in `step` (near `:614`) or inside `stepPlayer`.

## 5. Multiplayer / replica gating

**Replica (`replica: true`, `GameEngineOptions` `GameEngine.ts:201`, field `:228`):** `step` takes the early-return branch at **`GameEngine.ts:549-571`**. A replica runs **only**: local player motion prediction (`:554`), predictive mining for the crack overlay (`:559`), `recordTick` display stats (`:563`), `tickDayNight` (`:566`), `tickWeather` (`:567`), debug (`:568`). **Everything else is skipped** — mobs, spawns, random ticks, TNT, projectiles, breeding, raid, vitals — because it's replicated state written by `NetworkSession`, not simulated (comment `:543-548`).

# Implementation Plan: `feat/redstone-lite`

Player-buildable power circuits: lever, button (timed pop-back), pressure plate, redstone torch (inverter), redstone wire, and consumers (doors, TNT, a new glowing lamp). **Zero save bump (stays v17), zero worldgen bump (stays 11), zero binary assets, multiplayer rides the existing server-authoritative block-delta pipeline for free.** All verified facts from the brief re-confirmed against current source.

## 1. Design decisions (settled, with rationale)

### D1. Signal model: binary, BFS budget 15, slope-climbing wire
Binary on/off with a wire-step budget of `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE = 15` counted only across wire→wire hops. Gives the "wire runs out" feel with exactly **2 wire ids** instead of 16 strength variants (state-as-BlockId stays cheap). Wire connects to candidate wire neighbors at the 4 horizontal offsets **at the same Y and at ±1 Y** (8 probes/cell) — Minecraft-like slope climbing, unconditional (no "cut by block above" check; that refinement isn't worth the complexity in lite). Wire additionally *powers* all 6 face neighbors of its cell (that's how it powers a torch's support block, a door cell, a lamp, TNT).

### D2. Recompute: tracked-set + fixed-cadence full recompute + per-pass self-heal (option a)
- `state.redstone.cells: Set<voxelIndex>` — **session-only, never serialized**.
- **Seeded at boot** by scanning `state.blockChanges.changes()` for redstone-family ids. This is complete because every redstone block is craft-only ⇒ player-placed ⇒ present in the save diff (BrewingStand/Anvil precedent).
- **Maintained at exactly one seam**: successful placement in `placeSelectedBlock` calls `trackRedstoneCell`. No other producer needed.
- **Self-heal covers everything else**: each recompute pass iterates `cells` and drops any index whose current block is no longer a redstone id (mining, explosions, server-applied edits, any overwrite — none of them need to know redstone exists). It also pops any **overlay component whose support block vanished** (→ Air, no drop; the explosion that removed the support almost certainly vaporized the component too at blastResistance 0.4) and any **ButtonOn with no timer entry** (the post-reload heal — a save mid-press reloads pressed, first pass pops it back).
- **Fixed cadence**: an accumulator inside the redstone state runs the recompute every `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1` (engine dt ≤ `MAX_STEP_SECONDS` 0.05, so at most one recompute per step). This makes the torch clock deterministic (~0.2 s period for a 1-torch loop) instead of rAF-rate-dependent, and bounds cost to 10 Hz over player-scale circuits. No dirty flag: a full pass over a few-hundred-cell set at 10 Hz is trivial, and a stable circuit **writes nothing** (writes only on state change), so no remesh/relight/net traffic when idle.

### D3. Shapes, solidity, support
Six "overlay" (non-cube, non-colliding) ids — wire, lever×2, button×2, plate×2, torch×2 — plus the lamp as a plain full cube. Handling per function:

| Seam | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/world/meshing.ts` `pushBlockCuboid` (:217) | add `minY`/`maxY` params (door call site passes `0, 1`) |
| `lib/world/meshing.ts` block loop (:242) | `isRedstoneOverlay(block)` branch → `pushBlockCuboid` with `redstoneBounds(block)`; **no** neighbor culling (door precedent) |
| `lib/world/meshing.ts` cull condition (:254) | add `&& !isRedstoneOverlay(neighbor)` so faces behind a wire/lever aren't culled |
| `lib/world/queries.ts` `collidesAt` (:132) | `if (isRedstoneOverlay(block)) continue;` before the door branch — components never collide; players/mobs stand on the block below, feet occupying the plate cell (exactly what plate detection needs) |
| `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts` `highestSolidY` (:71) | exempt `isRedstoneOverlay` alongside `isDoorBlock` (spawn/mob ground finding) |
| `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts` `isSolid` | **unchanged** (stays true) — keeps `voxelRaycast` able to target components for mining/interact, same trade the doors made |
| `lib/world/lighting.ts` `opacity` (:49) | overlays → `0` (a wire must not black out its cell); lamp stays default-opaque (an opaque emitter, the Lava precedent) |

Bounds (in `redstoneBounds`, doors.ts-style): wire `y 0–0.07`, full x/z with 1/16 inset; plate `y 0–0.07` off / `0–0.04` on, 1/16 inset; button `0.3–0.7` x/z, `y 0–0.15` off / `0–0.08` on (pressed reads visually — on/off are different ids so different bounds are free); lever `0.35–0.65` x/z, `y 0–0.45` (handle direction painted per on/off tile); redstone torch `0.4–0.6` x/z, `y 0–0.65`.

**Placement rule** (all overlays): target cell Air/Water AND `world.isSolid(tx, ty-1, tz)` AND below is not itself an overlay/door. Refund-and-return on failure (door-branch precedent in `placeSelectedBlock`). **Support-break cascade**: in `tickMining`, after committing a break, if the cell above held an overlay, break it too and route its drop through `addBlockDrop` to the mining player (kelp-cascade precedent, mining.ts:182-193 — there is no ground-item entity in this game, so pop-off drops must be player-attributed or nothing).

### D4. Torch inverter semantics — no self-feedback by construction
A redstone torch sits on its support block (below). Rule: **a torch powers its 6 neighbors *except* its support cell**; **a torch's next state is OFF iff its support cell is in this pass's powered set**. Because a torch never powers its own support, no exclusion hack is needed — self-oscillation within one pass is impossible. The recompute is a synchronous single-pass update (all next-states computed from the current grid, then applied), i.e. a clocked cellular update at 10 Hz: a NOT gate has one 0.1 s delay; a torch clock oscillates at 5 Hz. Sane, deterministic, tunable via `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS`. (Real-MC "torch burnout" hysteresis: explicitly deferred.)

### D5. Doors: edge-triggered forcing
`state.redstone.prevDoorPowered: Set<lowerHalfIndex>` (session-only). Rising edge (newly powered) → force both halves open via `doorBlock(facing, true, ...)` + `doorToggled` emit; falling edge → force closed. Between edges, manual `interactDoor` works untouched — matching Minecraft (you *can* hand-close a powered door; the next power *edge* reclaims it) and never fighting the player at 10 Hz. Pair consistency reuses the doors.ts pair logic exactly as `interactDoor` does (interact.ts:89-101). A door is "powered" when either of its two cells is in the powered set (wire beside the door or a source/wire on the block next to it reaches it via the 6-neighbor powering rule).

### D6. Pressure plates: players AND mobs
Both — traps are the fun. Occupancy per pass: for each player, cell `(floor(px), floor(py + 0.05), floor(pz))` (feet cell — matches the collidesAt skip: feet rest in the plate cell); for each mob, `(floor(mx), floor(my − halfHeight + 0.05), floor(mz))` (**MobState.position is body center** — state.ts:125). Cost: |players| + |mobs| lookups at 10 Hz against a small plate subset of `cells`. Plate id flips on change only.

**tickRedstone pseudocode** (collect-then-apply, single `worldMeshDirty` — explosion.ts discipline; **never touches `drainEdits`**, which is the server's):

```
timer += dt; if timer < REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS return; timer = 0   // ≤1 pass per step
changed = false

// Phase 1 — inputs & self-heal (iterate cells; deletions safe on a Set)
occupied = feet cells of all players + all mobs (D6 formulas)
for idx of rs.cells:
  b = world.blocks[idx]
  if !isRedstoneBlock(b): cells.delete(idx); buttonTimers.delete(idx); continue
  if isRedstoneOverlay(b) && support below is not solid non-overlay:
      blockChanges.set(x,y,z, Air); cells.delete(idx); changed = true; continue   // orphan pop
  if isPlate(b) && (occupied.has(idx)) !== isRedstoneOn(b):
      blockChanges.set → flipped id; emit plateToggled{on}; changed = true
  if b === RedstoneButtonOn:
      t = buttonTimers.get(idx)                       // undefined after reload → heal
      if t === undefined || t - REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS <= 0:
          blockChanges.set → RedstoneButton; buttonTimers.delete; changed = true
      else buttonTimers.set(idx, t - REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS)

// Phase 2 — power graph from the CURRENT grid (post phase-1)
powered = Set(); wireBudget = Map<idx, number>; queue = []
for idx of cells where block ∈ {LeverOn, RedstoneButtonOn, PressurePlateOn, RedstoneTorch(on)}:
  for n of 6 neighbors, SKIPPING the below-neighbor when the source is a torch:   // D4
    powered.add(n)
    if isWire(block(n)): relaxBudget(n, REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE)
while queue: (w, budget) = pop
  powered.add(w); powered.add(each of w's 6 neighbors)          // wire powers what it touches
  if budget > 1: for c of 8 wire-step candidates (4 horiz × Y ∈ {0,+1,−1}):
    if isWire(block(c)): relaxBudget(c, budget − 1)             // keep best budget per cell
// relaxBudget: enqueue only if new budget > recorded budget (bounded, no revisits)

// Phase 3 — outputs (write only on change)
for idx of cells:
  b = block(idx)
  if isWire(b)          && (wireBudget.has(idx)) !== isRedstoneOn(b): flip; changed = true
  if isRedstoneLamp(b)  && powered.has(idx)      !== isRedstoneOn(b): flip; emit lampToggled{on}; changed = true
  if isRedstoneTorch*(b): want = !powered.has(idx below); if want !== isRedstoneOn(b): flip; changed = true
// Consumers OUTSIDE the tracked set — discovered by scanning the powered set:
doorPowered = Set()
for idx of powered:
  b = block(idx)
  if isDoorBlock(b): doorPowered.add(lower-half index via doorState)
  else if b === Tnt: primeTnt(state, x, y, z, emit)             // no-op if already lit
for lower of doorPowered − prevDoorPowered: force both halves open (doorBlock pair logic); emit doorToggled{open:true}; changed = true
for lower of prevDoorPowered − doorPowered: if still a door: force closed; emit doorToggled{open:false}; changed = true
prevDoorPowered = doorPowered

if changed: state.worldMeshDirty = true
```

Doors and TNT need **no tracking** — they're found through the powered set, so explosions/mining of consumers need zero bookkeeping.

# Implementation Plan: `feat/redstone-lite`

Player-buildable power circuits: lever, button (timed pop-back), pressure plate, redstone torch (inverter), redstone wire, and consumers (doors, TNT, a new glowing lamp). **Zero save bump (stays v17), zero worldgen bump (stays 11), zero binary assets, multiplayer rides the existing server-authoritative block-delta pipeline for free.** All verified facts from the brief re-confirmed against current source.

## 1. Design decisions (settled, with rationale)

### D1. Signal model: binary, BFS budget 15, slope-climbing wire
Binary on/off with a wire-step budget of `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE = 15` counted only across wire→wire hops. Gives the "wire runs out" feel with exactly **2 wire ids** instead of 16 strength variants (state-as-BlockId stays cheap). Wire connects to candidate wire neighbors at the 4 horizontal offsets **at the same Y and at ±1 Y** (8 probes/cell) — Minecraft-like slope climbing, unconditional (no "cut by block above" check; that refinement isn't worth the complexity in lite). Wire additionally *powers* all 6 face neighbors of its cell (that's how it powers a torch's support block, a door cell, a lamp, TNT).

### D2. Recompute: tracked-set + fixed-cadence full recompute + per-pass self-heal (option a)
- `state.redstone.cells: Set<voxelIndex>` — **session-only, never serialized**.
- **Seeded at boot** by scanning `state.blockChanges.changes()` for redstone-family ids. This is complete because every redstone block is craft-only ⇒ player-placed ⇒ present in the save diff (BrewingStand/Anvil precedent).
- **Maintained at exactly one seam**: successful placement in `placeSelectedBlock` calls `trackRedstoneCell`. No other producer needed.
- **Self-heal covers everything else**: each recompute pass iterates `cells` and drops any index whose current block is no longer a redstone id (mining, explosions, server-applied edits, any overwrite — none of them need to know redstone exists). It also pops any **overlay component whose support block vanished** (→ Air, no drop; the explosion that removed the support almost certainly vaporized the component too at blastResistance 0.4) and any **ButtonOn with no timer entry** (the post-reload heal — a save mid-press reloads pressed, first pass pops it back).
- **Fixed cadence**: an accumulator inside the redstone state runs the recompute every `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1` (engine dt ≤ `MAX_STEP_SECONDS` 0.05, so at most one recompute per step). This makes the torch clock deterministic (~0.2 s period for a 1-torch loop) instead of rAF-rate-dependent, and bounds cost to 10 Hz over player-scale circuits. No dirty flag: a full pass over a few-hundred-cell set at 10 Hz is trivial, and a stable circuit **writes nothing** (writes only on state change), so no remesh/relight/net traffic when idle.

### D3. Shapes, solidity, support
Six "overlay" (non-cube, non-colliding) ids — wire, lever×2, button×2, plate×2, torch×2 — plus the lamp as a plain full cube. Handling per function:

| Seam | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/world/meshing.ts` `pushBlockCuboid` (:217) | add `minY`/`maxY` params (door call site passes `0, 1`) |
| `lib/world/meshing.ts` block loop (:242) | `isRedstoneOverlay(block)` branch → `pushBlockCuboid` with `redstoneBounds(block)`; **no** neighbor culling (door precedent) |
| `lib/world/meshing.ts` cull condition (:254) | add `&& !isRedstoneOverlay(neighbor)` so faces behind a wire/lever aren't culled |
| `lib/world/queries.ts` `collidesAt` (:132) | `if (isRedstoneOverlay(block)) continue;` before the door branch — components never collide; players/mobs stand on the block below, feet occupying the plate cell (exactly what plate detection needs) |
| `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts` `highestSolidY` (:71) | exempt `isRedstoneOverlay` alongside `isDoorBlock` (spawn/mob ground finding) |
| `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts` `isSolid` | **unchanged** (stays true) — keeps `voxelRaycast` able to target components for mining/interact, same trade the doors made |
| `lib/world/lighting.ts` `opacity` (:49) | overlays → `0` (a wire must not black out its cell); lamp stays default-opaque (an opaque emitter, the Lava precedent) |

Bounds (in `redstoneBounds`, doors.ts-style): wire `y 0–0.07`, full x/z with 1/16 inset; plate `y 0–0.07` off / `0–0.04` on, 1/16 inset; button `0.3–0.7` x/z, `y 0–0.15` off / `0–0.08` on (pressed reads visually — on/off are different ids so different bounds are free); lever `0.35–0.65` x/z, `y 0–0.45` (handle direction painted per on/off tile); redstone torch `0.4–0.6` x/z, `y 0–0.65`.

**Placement rule** (all overlays): target cell Air/Water AND `world.isSolid(tx, ty-1, tz)` AND below is not itself an overlay/door. Refund-and-return on failure (door-branch precedent in `placeSelectedBlock`). **Support-break cascade**: in `tickMining`, after committing a break, if the cell above held an overlay, break it too and route its drop through `addBlockDrop` to the mining player (kelp-cascade precedent, mining.ts:182-193 — there is no ground-item entity in this game, so pop-off drops must be player-attributed or nothing).

### D4. Torch inverter semantics — no self-feedback by construction
A redstone torch sits on its support block (below). Rule: **a torch powers its 6 neighbors *except* its support cell**; **a torch's next state is OFF iff its support cell is in this pass's powered set**. Because a torch never powers its own support, no exclusion hack is needed — self-oscillation within one pass is impossible. The recompute is a synchronous single-pass update (all next-states computed from the current grid, then applied), i.e. a clocked cellular update at 10 Hz: a NOT gate has one 0.1 s delay; a torch clock oscillates at 5 Hz. Sane, deterministic, tunable via `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS`. (Real-MC "torch burnout" hysteresis: explicitly deferred.)

### D5. Doors: edge-triggered forcing
`state.redstone.prevDoorPowered: Set<lowerHalfIndex>` (session-only). Rising edge (newly powered) → force both halves open via `doorBlock(facing, true, ...)` + `doorToggled` emit; falling edge → force closed. Between edges, manual `interactDoor` works untouched — matching Minecraft (you *can* hand-close a powered door; the next power *edge* reclaims it) and never fighting the player at 10 Hz. Pair consistency reuses the doors.ts pair logic exactly as `interactDoor` does (interact.ts:89-101). A door is "powered" when either of its two cells is in the powered set (wire beside the door or a source/wire on the block next to it reaches it via the 6-neighbor powering rule).

### D6. Pressure plates: players AND mobs
Both — traps are the fun. Occupancy per pass: for each player, cell `(floor(px), floor(py + 0.05), floor(pz))` (feet cell — matches the collidesAt skip: feet rest in the plate cell); for each mob, `(floor(mx), floor(my − halfHeight + 0.05), floor(mz))` (**MobState.position is body center** — state.ts:125). Cost: |players| + |mobs| lookups at 10 Hz against a small plate subset of `cells`. Plate id flips on change only.

### D7. Recipes & progression (all from existing materials — worldgen deferral honored)
- **Redstone Dust**: `1 Gold Ore + 1 Coal → 8 Redstone Dust` — gold (conductor) is gated behind a tier-3 pick, coal is the powder carrier; 8/craft keeps wire affordable. *Explicit deferral note in CHANGELOG/docs: redstone ore worldgen comes with a future `WORLDGEN_VERSION` batch.*
- **Lever**: `1 Cobble + 1 Planks → 1 Lever`
- **Stone Button**: `1 Cobble → 2 Stone Button`
- **Pressure Plate**: `2 Planks → 1 Pressure Plate`
- **Redstone Torch**: `1 Redstone Dust + 1 Wood → 2 Redstone Torch` (mirrors the torch recipe shape)
- **Redstone Lamp**: `4 Redstone Dust + 2 Glass → 1 Redstone Lamp`

All results are `kind: "block"` ⇒ they land in the **Building** recipe-book category automatically (`KIND_TO_CATEGORY`, recipes.ts:677). Recommend *not* adding a "Redstone" category in lite (that touches `RecipeCategory` + order + `recipeCategory()`); flag as an open question. Item-source hints ("craft it") derive automatically from the recipes (`itemSources.ts`).

## 2. BlockId layout (exact — appended, ids 58–69)

Even = off, odd = on; `on(b) = b | 1`, `off(b) = b & ~1` (58 is even, so the parity trick is sound; contiguous family check `58 ≤ b ≤ 69`).

```ts
// lib/world/blocks.ts — append after CoralBlue = 57. Redstone-lite: power state is
// id-parity (even off / odd on) so toggles ride the save diff like doors do.
RedstoneWire = 58,      RedstoneWireOn = 59,
Lever = 60,             LeverOn = 61,
RedstoneButton = 62,    RedstoneButtonOn = 63,
PressurePlate = 64,     PressurePlateOn = 65,
RedstoneTorchOff = 66,  RedstoneTorch = 67,   // item places the LIT torch (67)
RedstoneLamp = 68,      RedstoneLampOn = 69
```

12 ids; ~186 remain free. Items place the even (off) variant except the torch (places 67). Uses no per-voxel aux state ⇒ **no save schema bump** (doors precedent); craft-only ⇒ **no WORLDGEN_VERSION bump** (Anvil precedent).

## 3. New modules

### `lib/world/redstone.ts` (mirrors doors.ts — pure id math + bounds, no engine imports)
```ts
export function isRedstoneBlock(b: number): b is BlockId;      // 58..69
export function isRedstoneOverlay(b: number): boolean;         // 58..67 (non-cube, non-colliding)
export function isRedstoneOn(b: number): boolean;              // family && (b & 1) === 1
export function redstoneOn(b: BlockId): BlockId;               // b | 1
export function redstoneOff(b: BlockId): BlockId;              // b & ~1
export function isWire/isLever/isButton/isPlate/isRedstoneTorch/isRedstoneLamp(b): boolean;
export type RedstoneBounds = { minX; maxX; minY; maxY; minZ; maxZ };
export function redstoneBounds(b: number): RedstoneBounds | null;
export const REDSTONE_PLACEABLE_OVERLAYS: readonly BlockId[];  // placement rule gate
```
Re-export the needed names from `lib/world/index.ts`.

### `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.ts` (the system)
```ts
export type RedstoneState = {
  cells: Set<number>;               // tracked redstone cells (session-only)
  buttonTimers: Map<number, number>;// pressed button → seconds left (primedTnt pattern)
  prevDoorPowered: Set<number>;     // lower-door indices powered last pass (edge detection)
  timer: number;                    // accumulator to REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS
};
export function createRedstoneState(): RedstoneState;
export function seedRedstoneCells(state: GameState): void;              // boot: scan blockChanges.changes()
export function trackRedstoneCell(state: GameState, x, y, z): void;     // placement seam
export function pressButton(state: GameState, x, y, z, emit): boolean;  // interact seam
export function toggleLever(state: GameState, x, y, z, emit): boolean;  // interact seam
export function tickRedstone(state: GameState, dt: number, emit: EmitGameEvent): void;
```

**tickRedstone pseudocode** (collect-then-apply, single `worldMeshDirty` — explosion.ts discipline; **never touches `drainEdits`**, which is the server's):

```
timer += dt; if timer < REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS return; timer = 0   // ≤1 pass per step
changed = false

// Phase 1 — inputs & self-heal (iterate cells; deletions safe on a Set)
occupied = feet cells of all players + all mobs (D6 formulas)
for idx of rs.cells:
  b = world.blocks[idx]
  if !isRedstoneBlock(b): cells.delete(idx); buttonTimers.delete(idx); continue
  if isRedstoneOverlay(b) && support below is not solid non-overlay:
      blockChanges.set(x,y,z, Air); cells.delete(idx); changed = true; continue   // orphan pop
  if isPlate(b) && (occupied.has(idx)) !== isRedstoneOn(b):
      blockChanges.set → flipped id; emit plateToggled{on}; changed = true
  if b === RedstoneButtonOn:
      t = buttonTimers.get(idx)                       // undefined after reload → heal
      if t === undefined || t - REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS <= 0:
          blockChanges.set → RedstoneButton; buttonTimers.delete; changed = true
      else buttonTimers.set(idx, t - REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS)

// Phase 2 — power graph from the CURRENT grid (post phase-1)
powered = Set(); wireBudget = Map<idx, number>; queue = []
for idx of cells where block ∈ {LeverOn, RedstoneButtonOn, PressurePlateOn, RedstoneTorch(on)}:
  for n of 6 neighbors, SKIPPING the below-neighbor when the source is a torch:   // D4
    powered.add(n)
    if isWire(block(n)): relaxBudget(n, REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE)
while queue: (w, budget) = pop
  powered.add(w); powered.add(each of w's 6 neighbors)          // wire powers what it touches
  if budget > 1: for c of 8 wire-step candidates (4 horiz × Y ∈ {0,+1,−1}):
    if isWire(block(c)): relaxBudget(c, budget − 1)             // keep best budget per cell
// relaxBudget: enqueue only if new budget > recorded budget (bounded, no revisits)

// Phase 3 — outputs (write only on change)
for idx of cells:
  b = block(idx)
  if isWire(b)          && (wireBudget.has(idx)) !== isRedstoneOn(b): flip; changed = true
  if isRedstoneLamp(b)  && powered.has(idx)      !== isRedstoneOn(b): flip; emit lampToggled{on}; changed = true
  if isRedstoneTorch*(b): want = !powered.has(idx below); if want !== isRedstoneOn(b): flip; changed = true
// Consumers OUTSIDE the tracked set — discovered by scanning the powered set:
doorPowered = Set()
for idx of powered:
  b = block(idx)
  if isDoorBlock(b): doorPowered.add(lower-half index via doorState)
  else if b === Tnt: primeTnt(state, x, y, z, emit)             // no-op if already lit
for lower of doorPowered − prevDoorPowered: force both halves open (doorBlock pair logic); emit doorToggled{open:true}; changed = true
for lower of prevDoorPowered − doorPowered: if still a door: force closed; emit doorToggled{open:false}; changed = true
prevDoorPowered = doorPowered

if changed: state.worldMeshDirty = true
```

Doors and TNT need **no tracking** — they're found through the powered set, so explosions/mining of consumers need zero bookkeeping.

## 5. Save / reload / self-heal summary

- Power state = id parity; lever/plate/wire/lamp/torch states persist in the diff and are **re-derived to consistency within one redstone tick of load** (first pass recomputes everything from the grid).
- Pressed button + empty `buttonTimers` after reload → popped back on first pass (§D2).
- `prevDoorPowered` empty after reload → a still-powered door registers as a rising edge and re-forces open (idempotent if already open — write-on-change suppresses the churn; emit doorToggled only when a cell actually flips).
- Explosion/mining destroying circuit cells → self-heal deletion; orphaned overlays popped.

## 6. Test plan

Inert content — nothing obtainable yet.
2. `feat(items): redstone items, drops, recipes` — items.ts, recipes.ts, config.test additions ride automatically.

4. `feat(audio): switch click routing` — soundParams.ts, audioDirector.ts (+tests).
5. `docs: redstone-lite manual/reference/tuning/testing + CHANGELOG`.

## 9. Verification checklist

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` (meshing/renderer touched).

## 10. Risks & open questions

**Risks**
- **Clock churn**: an oscillating circuit sets `worldMeshDirty` + relights + broadcasts a handful of block deltas every 0.1–0.2 s. Same cost class as mining spam and bounded by circuit size; stable circuits cost zero (write-on-change). Flagged in tuning.md; `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS` is the throttle.

# Redstone-lite

## Context

The game's most conspicuous content absence is player-buildable power circuits — no levers, buttons, plates, wire, or logic anywhere, while every natural consumer (doors, TNT, the lighting engine) already exists. This branch adds a deliberately "lite" redstone system: sources (lever, button with timed pop-back, pressure plate, redstone torch), a conductor (wire), and consumers (doors, TNT ignition, a new glowing lamp). The torch acts as an inverter, so NOT gates and clocks are buildable. Explicitly out of scope: pistons, repeaters/comparators, redstone-ore worldgen (a `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump discards existing worlds' block diffs — deferred to a future worldgen batch; noted in CHANGELOG), signal-strength visuals, wall-mounted components (floor-mount only; facing variants can be added later as new ids).

**Hard guarantees: no save schema bump (stays v17), no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump (stays 11), zero binary assets, zero multiplayer wire code** — power state is encoded as BlockId variants (the doors precedent rides the save diff for free), all blocks are craft-only appended ids (Anvil precedent), and the tick system runs server-only automatically (replicas early-return in `GameEngine.step` at `:549`; server edits replicate through the existing `drainEdits → TickMessage.blocks` journal like TNT craters already do).

Branch: `feat/redstone-lite` off `main`.

## User decisions

- **Dedicated "Redstone" recipe-book category** (user-picked): extend the `RecipeCategory` union + category ordering + the categorization logic in `lib/game/recipes.ts` (block-kind results currently auto-map to Building via `KIND_TO_CATEGORY` ~:677 — the six redstone recipes need an explicit category override), and whatever `InventoryPanel` section rendering/tests assume about the category list.
- Defaults taken while user was AFK (flip on request): dust recipe `1 Gold Ore + 1 Coal → 8 Redstone Dust` (mid-game gate behind a tier-3 pick); one **"Circuit Breaker"** advancement (first lever toggle — two declarative registry entries in `advancements.ts`, zero logic); **single** pressure plate (2 planks) triggered by players AND mobs; lamp emission 15, redstone torch 7.

## Block ids (append after `CoralBlue = 57`; even = off, odd = on; `on = b|1`, `off = b&~1` — 58 is even so parity works)

```
RedstoneWire = 58,      RedstoneWireOn = 59,
Lever = 60,             LeverOn = 61,
RedstoneButton = 62,    RedstoneButtonOn = 63,
PressurePlate = 64,     PressurePlateOn = 65,
RedstoneTorchOff = 66,  RedstoneTorch = 67,   // item places the LIT torch
RedstoneLamp = 68,      RedstoneLampOn = 69
```

Ids 58–67 are "overlays" (non-cube, non-colliding); the lamp is a plain full cube (opaque emitter, Lava precedent).

## Core design

- **Signal model**: binary on/off; BFS through wire with budget `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE = 15` counted on wire→wire hops (the "wire runs out" feel with only 2 wire ids). Wire steps to the 4 horizontal neighbors at Y and Y±1 (slope climbing); a wire cell *powers* all 6 face neighbors. Sources power their 6 neighbors — except a torch never powers its own support cell.
- **Torch inverter**: next state OFF iff its support cell is powered this pass. Since a torch never powers its support, no self-feedback is possible. Single synchronous pass per redstone tick = clocked update; a torch clock oscillates at 2×`REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS`.
- **Recompute**: `state.redstone` (session-only, like `primedTnt`): `cells: Set<voxelIndex>` (tracked components), `buttonTimers: Map<idx, seconds>`, `prevDoorPowered: Set<lowerIdx>`, `timer`. Seeded at boot by scanning `state.blockChanges.changes()` (craft-only ⇒ every redstone cell is in the diff); maintained only by the placement seam; **self-heals** each pass by dropping any tracked index that no longer holds a redstone id (mining/explosions/server edits need zero redstone awareness) and popping orphaned overlays whose support vanished. Fixed cadence `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1` via accumulator (engine `MAX_STEP_SECONDS` is 0.05 → ≤1 pass/step). Writes only on state change → a stable circuit costs zero remesh/relight/net traffic.
- **Tick phases** (collect-then-apply, one `worldMeshDirty` per changed pass; NEVER touches `drainEdits` — that's the server's): (1) inputs + self-heal — plate occupancy (players' feet cell `floor(py+0.05)`; mobs at body-center minus half-height), button countdown + pop-back (a ButtonOn with no timer entry — i.e. after reload — pops immediately: self-heal); (2) power graph BFS from on-sources over the current grid with per-cell best-budget relaxation; (3) outputs — flip wire/lamp/torch ids on change; scan the powered set for consumers: doors (edge-triggered: rising edge forces both halves open via the `doorBlock` pair logic, falling edge forces closed, manual `interactDoor` untouched between edges) and TNT (`primeTnt`, already idempotent). Doors/TNT need no tracking — discovered via the powered set.
- **Shapes/collision**: extend `pushBlockCuboid` (meshing.ts:217) with `minY`/`maxY` (door call site passes `0, 1`; corners currently hardcode `y + cy`); overlay mesh branch + neighbor-cull exemption mirror the door branch (:242, :254). `collidesAt` (queries.ts:132) skips overlays (walk over wire/plates; feet occupy the plate cell — exactly what detection needs); `highestSolidY` (voxelWorld.ts:71) exempts overlays; `isSolid` unchanged (keeps `voxelRaycast` targeting them, the door trade-off). `opacity()` → 0 for overlays; `emission()`: RedstoneTorch 7, RedstoneLampOn 15 — toggles relight automatically because every id swap goes through `blockChanges.set → applyEdit`.
- **Placement/breaking**: overlays require Air/Water target + solid non-overlay below, refund-and-return otherwise (door-branch pattern in `placeSelectedBlock`); after any successful redstone placement call `trackRedstoneCell`. Breaking a support block cascades the overlay above with a player-attributed drop (kelp-cascade precedent, mining.ts:182-193).

## Files

**New**: `lib/world/redstone.ts` (pure id math + `redstoneBounds`, doors.ts mirror; re-export via `lib/world/index.ts`), `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.ts` (`createRedstoneState`, `seedRedstoneCells`, `trackRedstoneCell`, `pressButton`, `toggleLever`, `tickRedstone`).

**Touched**: `lib/world/blocks.ts` (12 enum ids + `BLOCK_COLORS` for all 12 — atlas auto-sizes off this map, missing entry = garbage UVs — + `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` for the 6 placeables); `lib/world/atlas.ts` (12 paint branches; lamp = dull ochre off / bright saturated on — the shader's existing block-light glow term does the rest, no renderer change); `lib/world/meshing.ts`; `lib/world/lighting.ts`; `lib/world/queries.ts`; `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts`; `lib/game/items.ts` (`ITEM_DEFS` ×6 block-kind — auto isometric icons, no sprites; `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` ×12 with on/off → same item; `BREAK_HARDNESS` overlays 1 / lamp 3); `lib/game/recipes.ts` (6 recipes + the new Redstone category); `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` (12 exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` entries — typecheck fails until present: wire sand, lever/torch wood, button/plate stone, lamp glass); `lib/game/audio/soundParams.ts` (+`switchClick` ZZFX def) + `audioDirector.ts` (route `leverToggled`/`buttonPressed`/`plateToggled`; `doorToggled`/`tntPrimed` already handled); `lib/game/engine/state.ts` (`GameState.redstone` + 4 `GameEvent` variants); `interact.ts` (`InteractiveKind` + `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` + lever/button branches); `mining.ts` (placement rule + cascade + tracking); `GameEngine.ts` (state init; `seedRedstoneCells` after `applySavedChanges`; `tickRedstone(state, dt, this.emit)` between `tickMobs` :618 and `tickPrimedTnt` :619 — after the player loop so this frame's interactions are visible, before the fuse countdown so wire→TNT ignites same tick); `lib/game/config.ts` (`REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1`, `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE = 15`, `REDSTONE_BUTTON_PRESS_SECONDS = 1.0`); `advancements.ts` (lever stat + "Circuit Breaker"); `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` only if the category list is enumerated there.

## Tests

- `lib/world/redstone.test.ts` (doors.test.ts mirror): parity math, predicates, bounds for every overlay id.
- `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.test.ts` (headless, explosion.test.ts pattern): lever→wire→lamp on/off; budget boundary (15th powers, 16th doesn't); slope continuity; torch inverts + never self-feeds; clock oscillates at 2×tick; button pop-back + reload heal; plate under player and mob, releases on vacate; door rising/falling edges + manual toggle between edges; powered TNT primes; self-heal on overwritten cell; orphan pop on support break; **stable circuit performs zero writes across passes**.
- Cases added to: `lighting.test.ts` (lamp emission, overlay opacity), `mining.test.ts` (support rule + refund, cascade drop), `interact.test.ts` (lever/button consume the click), `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (server lever flip lands in `drainEdits`; replica never runs `tickRedstone`), recipes/InventoryPanel tests for the new category.
- No new e2e scenario (fully headless-testable), but run `bun run test:e2e` — meshing/renderer touched.

## Docs (ship with the change)

`docs/manual.md` new Redstone section (incl. NOT gate + clock how-to); `docs/reference.md` blocks/items/recipes tables + the new category; `docs/adding-content.md` (overlay-bounds seam + powered-component pattern); `docs/tuning.md` (3 tunables with trade-offs); `docs/testing.md` (2 new suite rows); `docs/architecture.md` (step-order line + server-only note); `CHANGELOG.md` (explicitly: no save/worldgen impact; redstone-ore deferral).

## Commits (each lint/typecheck/test-green)

1. `feat(world): redstone blocks, overlay meshing, lighting` — blocks/redstone.ts/atlas/meshing (incl. minY/maxY refactor)/lighting/queries/voxelWorld/materials + redstone.test.ts (content inert, nothing obtainable).
2. `feat(items): redstone items, recipes, Redstone category` — items/recipes (+category UI seam).
3. `feat(engine): redstone power system` — state/systems/redstone.ts/interact/mining/GameEngine/config/advancements + system tests.
4. `feat(audio): switch click routing` — soundParams/audioDirector + tests.
5. `docs: redstone-lite` — docs + CHANGELOG.

## Verification

- Full gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`, `bun run test:e2e` (check `lsof -i :3000` first). Confirm: `generation.ts` untouched (worldgen hash tests must NOT re-baseline), no `public/` additions, a pre-feature v17 save loads unchanged.
- Manual visual pass (`bun run dev`, user): atlas tiles read (on/off contrast), overlays sit flush (wire flat, pressed button lower), lamp glows in the dark, no movement snag on wire/plates, plate triggers underfoot, lever/button sounds, NOT gate + 2-torch clock behave, wire fires TNT, powered door opens and hand-closes between edges. Multiplayer spot-check per docs/online.md: guest sees host's lever flip with ≤1-tick lag.

## Risks

- Oscillating clocks cost a remesh + a few block deltas per 0.1–0.2 s (mining-spam cost class, bounded by circuit size; stable circuits cost zero; `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS` is the throttle — documented in tuning.md).
- `pushBlockCuboid` signature change touches the door path — mechanical refactor, covered by existing door meshing tests.
- AO/ground-finding treat overlay cells as solid in two cosmetic spots — matches the door trade-off, accepted.

# Redstone-lite

## Context

The game's most conspicuous content absence is player-buildable power circuits — no levers, buttons, plates, wire, or logic anywhere, while every natural consumer (doors, TNT, the lighting engine) already exists. This branch adds a deliberately "lite" redstone system: sources (lever, button with timed pop-back, pressure plate, redstone torch), a conductor (wire), and consumers (doors, TNT ignition, a new glowing lamp). The torch acts as an inverter, so NOT gates and clocks are buildable. Explicitly out of scope: pistons, repeaters/comparators, redstone-ore worldgen (a `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump discards existing worlds' block diffs — deferred to a future worldgen batch; noted in CHANGELOG), signal-strength visuals, wall-mounted components (floor-mount only; facing variants can be added later as new ids).

**Hard guarantees: no save schema bump (stays v17), no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump (stays 11), zero binary assets, zero multiplayer wire code** — power state is encoded as BlockId variants (the doors precedent rides the save diff for free), all blocks are craft-only appended ids (Anvil precedent), and the tick system runs server-only automatically (replicas early-return in `GameEngine.step` at `:549`; server edits replicate through the existing `drainEdits → TickMessage.blocks` journal like TNT craters already do).

Branch: `feat/redstone-lite` off `main`.

## User decisions

- **Dedicated "Redstone" recipe-book category** (user-picked): extend the `RecipeCategory` union + category ordering + the categorization logic in `lib/game/recipes.ts` (block-kind results currently auto-map to Building via `KIND_TO_CATEGORY` ~:677 — the six redstone recipes need an explicit category override), and whatever `InventoryPanel` section rendering/tests assume about the category list.
- **Dust recipe `1 Gold Ore + 1 Coal → 8 Redstone Dust`** (user-picked): mid-game gate behind a tier-3 pick.
- **One "Circuit Breaker" advancement** (user-picked): unlocked on first lever toggle — two declarative registry entries in `advancements.ts`, zero logic.
- Defaults (user AFK on these; flip on request): **single** pressure plate (2 planks) triggered by players AND mobs; lamp emission 15, redstone torch 7.

## Block ids (append after `CoralBlue = 57`; even = off, odd = on; `on = b|1`, `off = b&~1` — 58 is even so parity works)

```
RedstoneWire = 58,      RedstoneWireOn = 59,
Lever = 60,             LeverOn = 61,
RedstoneButton = 62,    RedstoneButtonOn = 63,
PressurePlate = 64,     PressurePlateOn = 65,
RedstoneTorchOff = 66,  RedstoneTorch = 67,   // item places the LIT torch
RedstoneLamp = 68,      RedstoneLampOn = 69
```

Ids 58–67 are "overlays" (non-cube, non-colliding); the lamp is a plain full cube (opaque emitter, Lava precedent).

## Core design

- **Signal model**: binary on/off; BFS through wire with budget `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE = 15` counted on wire→wire hops (the "wire runs out" feel with only 2 wire ids). Wire steps to the 4 horizontal neighbors at Y and Y±1 (slope climbing); a wire cell *powers* all 6 face neighbors. Sources power their 6 neighbors — except a torch never powers its own support cell.
- **Torch inverter**: next state OFF iff its support cell is powered this pass. Since a torch never powers its support, no self-feedback is possible. Single synchronous pass per redstone tick = clocked update; a torch clock oscillates at 2×`REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS`.
- **Recompute**: `state.redstone` (session-only, like `primedTnt`): `cells: Set<voxelIndex>` (tracked components), `buttonTimers: Map<idx, seconds>`, `prevDoorPowered: Set<lowerIdx>`, `timer`. Seeded at boot by scanning `state.blockChanges.changes()` (craft-only ⇒ every redstone cell is in the diff); maintained only by the placement seam; **self-heals** each pass by dropping any tracked index that no longer holds a redstone id (mining/explosions/server edits need zero redstone awareness) and popping orphaned overlays whose support vanished. Fixed cadence `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1` via accumulator (engine `MAX_STEP_SECONDS` is 0.05 → ≤1 pass/step). Writes only on state change → a stable circuit costs zero remesh/relight/net traffic.
- **Tick phases** (collect-then-apply, one `worldMeshDirty` per changed pass; NEVER touches `drainEdits` — that's the server's): (1) inputs + self-heal — plate occupancy (players' feet cell `floor(py+0.05)`; mobs at body-center minus half-height), button countdown + pop-back (a ButtonOn with no timer entry — i.e. after reload — pops immediately: self-heal); (2) power graph BFS from on-sources over the current grid with per-cell best-budget relaxation; (3) outputs — flip wire/lamp/torch ids on change; scan the powered set for consumers: doors (edge-triggered: rising edge forces both halves open via the `doorBlock` pair logic, falling edge forces closed, manual `interactDoor` untouched between edges) and TNT (`primeTnt`, already idempotent). Doors/TNT need no tracking — discovered via the powered set.
- **Shapes/collision**: extend `pushBlockCuboid` (meshing.ts:217) with `minY`/`maxY` (door call site passes `0, 1`; corners currently hardcode `y + cy`); overlay mesh branch + neighbor-cull exemption mirror the door branch (:242, :254). `collidesAt` (queries.ts:132) skips overlays (walk over wire/plates; feet occupy the plate cell — exactly what detection needs); `highestSolidY` (voxelWorld.ts:71) exempts overlays; `isSolid` unchanged (keeps `voxelRaycast` targeting them, the door trade-off). `opacity()` → 0 for overlays; `emission()`: RedstoneTorch 7, RedstoneLampOn 15 — toggles relight automatically because every id swap goes through `blockChanges.set → applyEdit`.
- **Placement/breaking**: overlays require Air/Water target + solid non-overlay below, refund-and-return otherwise (door-branch pattern in `placeSelectedBlock`); after any successful redstone placement call `trackRedstoneCell`. 4

34	- **Torch inverter**: next state OFF iff its support cell is powered this pass. Since a torch never powers its support, no self-feedback is possible. Single synchronous pass per redstone tick = clocked update; a torch clock oscillates at 2×`REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS`.

- `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.test.ts` (headless, explosion.test.ts pattern): lever→wire→lamp on/off; budget boundary (15th powers, 16th doesn't); slope continuity; torch inverts + never self-feeds; clock oscillates at 2×tick; button pop-back + reload heal; plate under player and mob, releases on vacate; door rising/falling edges + manual toggle between edges; powered TNT primes; self-heal on overwritten cell; orphan pop on support break; **stable circuit performs zero writes across passes**.
- Cases added to: `lighting.test.ts` (lamp emission, overlay opacity), `mining.test.ts` (support rule + refund, cascade drop), `interact.test.ts` (lever/button consume the click), `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (server lever flip lands in `drainEdits`; replica never runs `tickRedstone`), recipe-table tests pick up the six new entries.
- No new e2e scenario (fully headless-testable), but run `bun run test:e2e` — meshing/renderer touched.

## Docs (ship with the change)

`docs/manual.md` new Redstone section (incl. NOT gate + clock how-to); `docs/reference.md` blocks/items/recipes tables + the new category; `docs/adding-content.md` (overlay-bounds seam + powered-component pattern); `docs/tuning.md` (3 tunables with trade-offs); `docs/testing.md` (2 new suite rows); `docs/architecture.md` (step-order line + server-only note); `CHANGELOG.md` (explicitly: no save/worldgen impact; redstone-ore deferral).

## Commits (each lint/typecheck/test-green)

1. `feat(world): redstone blocks, overlay meshing, lighting` — blocks/redstone.ts/atlas/meshing (incl. minY/maxY refactor)/lighting/queries/voxelWorld/materials + redstone.test.ts (content inert, nothing obtainable).
2. `feat(items): redstone items and recipes` — items/recipes.
3. `feat(engine): redstone power system` — state/systems/redstone.ts/interact/mining/GameEngine/config/advancements + system tests.
4. `feat(audio): switch click routing` — soundParams/audioDirector + tests.
5. `docs: redstone-lite` — docs + CHANGELOG.

## Verification

- Full gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`, `bun run test:e2e` (check `lsof -i :3000` first). Confirm: `generation.ts` untouched (worldgen hash tests must NOT re-baseline), no `public/` additions, a pre-feature v17 save loads unchanged.
- Manual visual pass (`bun run dev`, user): atlas tiles read (on/off contrast), overlays sit flush (wire flat, pressed button lower), lamp glows in the dark, no movement snag on wire/plates, plate triggers underfoot, lever/button sounds, NOT gate + 2-torch clock behave, wire fires TNT, powered door opens and hand-closes between edges. Multiplayer spot-check per docs/online.md: guest sees host's lever flip with ≤1-tick lag.

## Risks

- Oscillating clocks cost a remesh + a few block deltas per 0.1–0.2 s (mining-spam cost class, bounded by circuit size; stable circuits cost zero; `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS` is the throttle — documented in tuning.md).
- `pushBlockCuboid` signature change touches the door path — mechanical refactor, covered by existing door meshing tests.
- AO/ground-finding treat overlay cells as solid in two cosmetic spots — matches the door trade-off, accepted.

export const WORLD_SIZE_X = 512;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Y = 150;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Z = 512;

export const enum BlockId {
  Air = 0,
  Grass = 1,
  Dirt = 2,
  Stone = 3,
  Wood = 4,
  Leaves = 5,
  Bedrock = 6,
  Planks = 7,
  Cobblestone = 8,
  Sand = 9,
  Brick = 10,
  Glass = 11,
  SliverOre = 12,
  RubyOre = 13,
  GoldOre = 14,
  SapphireOre = 15,
  DiamondOre = 16,
  Water = 17,
  Snow = 18,
  Cactus = 19,
  Bed = 20,
  Farmland = 21,
  // Wheat growth stages — consecutive ids so a crop advances by +1 (see randomTicks.ts).
  WheatStage0 = 22,
  WheatStage1 = 23,
  WheatStage2 = 24,
  WheatStage3 = 25,
  Furnace = 26,
  Chest = 27,
  // Dungeon blocks (worldgen-only flavor + the spawner block-entity marker).
  MossyCobblestone = 28,
  Spawner = 29,
  // Wood doors — 16 contiguous ids (4 facings × open/closed × lower/upper).
  // doors.ts derives state by offset from DoorNorthLower, so keep them in order.
  DoorNorthLower = 30,
  DoorNorthUpper = 31,
  DoorEastLower = 32,
  DoorEastUpper = 33,
  DoorSouthLower = 34,
  DoorSouthUpper = 35,
  DoorWestLower = 36,
  DoorWestUpper = 37,
  DoorNorthOpenLower = 38,
  DoorNorthOpenUpper = 39,
  DoorEastOpenLower = 40,
  DoorEastOpenUpper = 41,
  DoorSouthOpenLower = 42,
  DoorSouthOpenUpper = 43,
  DoorWestOpenLower = 44,
  DoorWestOpenUpper = 45,
  // A placeable light source: a solid block that emits block light (see lighting.ts).
  Torch = 46,
  // A worldgen-only hazard: a solid, unmineable block that emits max block light
  // and burns the player on contact (see lighting.ts, playerStats.ts).
  Lava = 47,
  // A shallow, common ore: mineable with a wood pickaxe, drops coal (furnace fuel).
  CoalOre = 48,
  // A placeable explosive: right-click with a torch to ignite a fuse, then it blows.
  Tnt = 49,
  // A young tree: plant on grass/dirt, grows into a tree over time (random ticks)
  // or instantly with bone meal. A solid cube like wheat (see atlas.ts).
  Sapling = 50,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open its brewing recipes (potions). Like
  // the furnace, it gates `station: "brewing"` recipes (see interact.ts).
  BrewingStand = 51,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the enchanting panel, where XP levels
  // are spent to enchant the held tool/weapon/armor (see interact.ts).
  EnchantingTable = 52,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the anvil panel, where XP levels are
  // spent to repair, combine, or rename the held gear (see interact.ts).
  Anvil = 53,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the grindstone panel, which strips a
  // held item's enchantments and refunds some XP (see interact.ts).
  Grindstone = 54,
  // Ocean flora. Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (like wheat)
  // that generates in stalks on the ocean floor and grows upward through water
  // via random ticks; breaking one cell breaks the stalk above it (mining.ts).
  Kelp = 55,
  // Decorative reef blocks scattered on the ocean floor (worldgen only).
  CoralPink = 56,
  CoralBlue = 57,
  // Redstone-lite (see redstone.ts). Power state is id PARITY — even = off,
  // odd = on (`b | 1` / `b & ~1`) — so toggles ride the save diff like doors.
  // Ids 58-67 are floor-mounted "overlays": non-cube, non-colliding shapes
  // meshed via redstoneBounds. The lamp pair is a plain full cube.
  RedstoneWire = 58,
  RedstoneWireOn = 59,
  Lever = 60,
  LeverOn = 61,
  RedstoneButton = 62,
  RedstoneButtonOn = 63,
  PressurePlate = 64,
  PressurePlateOn = 65,
  // The torch item places the LIT variant; the power pass turns it off when
  // its support block is powered (the inverter rule).
  RedstoneTorchOff = 66,
  RedstoneTorch = 67,
  RedstoneLamp = 68,
  RedstoneLampOn = 69
}

the blockChanges.set chokepoint exactly like a door does - no save or

sit visibly lower when pressed; collidesAt skips overlays so players
walk over wire and stand IN a plate's cell (what detection needs), and
highestSolidY exempts them like doors. Overlays are light-transparent;
the lit torch emits 7 and the powered lamp 15 - emission follows the id,
so the power system toggles light by swapping ids.

Nothing is craftable or placeable yet; the items, recipes, and the
power simulation land in the next slices.
EOF

feat(engine): redstone power system

The simulation half of redstone-lite: tickRedstone runs a fixed-cadence
(REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS) power pass between tickMobs and tickPrimedTnt -
after the player loop so this frame's lever/button clicks are visible,
before the fuse countdown so wire-lit TNT starts ticking the same frame.

The pass re-derives power from the block grid every time: on-sources
(lever, pressed button/plate, lit redstone torch) power their six face
neighbors, wire BFSes outward with a REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE hop budget and
one-block slope climbing, and consumers respond - lamps light, TNT
primes, doors force open/closed on power edges (manual toggling still
works between edges). The torch never powers its own support and turns
off while that support is powered, which yields inverters and two-pass
clocks with no oscillation hazard inside a pass.

Bookkeeping is a tracked cell set fed by one seam (placement) and
seeded at boot from the block diff (craft-only blocks are always
player-placed, so the diff is a complete census); everything else
self-heals per pass - overwritten cells drop out, orphaned overlays pop,
a mid-press save reloads with its button healed shut. Writes happen only
on state change, so a stable circuit costs zero remesh/relight/net
traffic. Replicas never run the system; server passes replicate through
the existing block journal, verified by the new multiplayer tests.

Also: lever/button right-click routing in interact.ts, the overlay
support rule + refund and the support-break cascade in mining.ts, and
the "Circuit Breaker" advancement on the first lever flip.
EOF

## Doors

Craft a **wood door** from **6 planks** and place it on a solid floor with two
clear blocks above it. A door is a thin, two-block-tall panel: right-click either
half to open or close the whole door. Closed doors block players and mobs; open
doors rotate against their hinge so you can pass. Mobs cannot open or close doors.
Breaking either half removes the whole door and returns one door item.

## Storage

Your pack only holds 36 slots, so build **chests** to stash the overflow. Craft a
chest from **8 planks**, place it, and **right-click** it to open it: a **27-slot**
grid appears above your inventory. Move items the same way you rearrange the
inventory — **click a slot, then click where it should go** — across either grid.
Close the panel (`I` or `Esc`) and the chest keeps its contents, which are **saved
with your world**.

Breaking a chest doesn't destroy what's inside: its contents **spill back into your
inventory** (and you get the chest item back). If your inventory is too full to hold
everything, the break is refused and the chest stays put — empty it a bit first.

## Redstone

Build **power circuits** that open doors, light lamps, and set off TNT. Craft
**Redstone Dust** from **1 gold ore + 1 coal** (→ 8 dust — you'll need a
sliver-tier pickaxe to reach gold), then wire up:

- **Sources** make power: a **lever** (right-click to toggle), a **stone button**
  (right-click for a ~1-second pulse), a **pressure plate** (press by standing on
  it — mobs trigger plates too, so traps work), and a **redstone torch** (always
  on... see below).
- **Redstone dust** places as **wire**: a flat trail that carries power up to
  **15 blocks** from a source, climbing single-block steps. Powered wire glows
  red. Wire, levers, buttons, plates, and torches all mount on top of a solid
  block and pop off (dropping their item) if you break the block under them.
- **Consumers** react to power: a **door** next to a powered wire is forced open
  (and closes when the power drops — you can still open/close it by hand in
  between), **TNT** ignites its fuse, and the new **redstone lamp**
  (4 dust + 2 glass) lights up like a torch you can switch.

The **redstone torch** (1 dust + 1 wood → 2) is the clever piece: it powers its
neighbors like a tiny always-on source, **unless the block it stands on is
powered — then it turns off**. That inversion is a **NOT gate**: lever → wire →
torch's base block, and the torch's output is the opposite of the lever. Feed a
torch's output back to its own base through a wire loop and it blinks — a
**clock** for flashing lamps. Circuits update on a fixed ~0.1 s tick, so signals
ripple visibly through long contraptions.

## Storage

Your pack only holds 36 slots, so build **chests** to stash the overflow.

## Recipes

**74 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).
All use the always-available crafting grid except the **furnace** smelting recipes
(need an open furnace) and the eight **brewing** recipes (need an open
[brewing stand](#brewing--potions)).

In-game, the recipe book groups recipes into the sections below (Tools, Vehicles,
Weapons, Armor, Building, Food, Materials, then Smelting, Brewing, and Trades), listing the
recipes you can currently afford first within each section. Hovering a recipe you
can't afford shows each ingredient as have / need plus a "how to obtain it" hint
for the missing ones (derived from the loot/recipe tables in `itemSources.ts`).

### Building & materials

| Result             | Ingredients              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| 4 Planks           | 2 Wood                   |
| 2 Glass            | 4 Sand                   |
| 2 Brick            | 2 Dirt + 2 Stone         |
| 1 Furnace          | 8 Cobble                 |
| 1 Chest            | 8 Planks                 |
| 1 Brewing Stand    | 3 Cobble + 1 Gold Ore    |
| 1 Enchanting Table | 2 Diamond Ore + 4 Cobble |
| 1 Anvil            | 3 Gold Ore + 4 Cobble    |
| 1 Grindstone       | 2 Cobble + 2 Planks      |
| 1 Wood Door        | 6 Planks                 |
| 4 Torch            | 1 Coal + 1 Wood          |
| 1 Bed              | 3 Wool + 3 Planks        |
| 1 Wool             | 4 String                 |
| 1 TNT              | 4 Gunpowder + 1 Sand     |
| 3 Bone Meal        | 1 Bone                   |
| 3 Glass Bottle     | 3 Glass                  |

### Tools

| Result           | Ingredients             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- |
| Wood Hoe         | 2 Planks + 1 Wood       |
| Fishing Rod      | 3 Wood + 2 String       |

content.content:
### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)

0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
1. Stuck detection / auto-unstuck (`STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`)
2. Death check + respawn countdown (while dead, only mobs tick)
3. Sleep gate: while `state.sleepTimer > 0`, `step` decrements the fade and returns (full freeze, like pause); at zero it skips the clock to the next morning
4. Player or mounted-vehicle movement (`systems/playerMotion.ts` / `systems/vehicles.ts` — walking derives direction from `yaw`; mounted rafts/ships carry the player and check water support)
5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
6. Mining progress and block breaking (`systems/mining.ts`; placement also lives here)
7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula); immediately after, `systems/weather.ts` sets the **transient** `state.weather` (rain/snow/clear) as a pure function of `dayClock` + seed — cosmetic only: never serialized, never touches spawn/daylight balance
8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)

content.content:
**Vehicles.** Rafts and ships are persistent logical entities (`VehicleState`) rather than blocks. `systems/vehicles.ts` owns water-surface placement, right-click boarding for rafts, step-on boarding for ships, mounted steering, dismount selection, water-support checks, and v16 save restore filtering. The rider link is session-only; placed vehicles persist through `SaveData.vehicles`.

**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.

**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new kind requires entries in all seven exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND`, `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).

content.content:
## A new block

1. Add to the `BlockId` enum and `BLOCK_COLORS` in `lib/world/blocks.ts` — the atlas auto-generates its tile. Add a `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` entry for the first-person model tint.
2. Add a `BREAK_HARDNESS` entry in `lib/game/items.ts` (omitted blocks default to hardness 2).
3. Make it placeable/droppable: an `ITEM_DEFS` entry (`kind: "block"`, `blockId`) plus a `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` mapping — without the mapping, mining it drops nothing. The inventory icon (isometric cube) auto-generates from `BLOCK_COLORS`; ore-style blocks can add an accent color in `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts` (`ORE_ACCENTS`).
4. Optionally add `RECIPES` entries in `lib/game/recipes.ts`.
5. Non-cube, non-solid, or transparent blocks need engine work: collision in `lib/world/queries.ts` / `voxelWorld.ts` and geometry/face visibility in `lib/world/meshing.ts`. Doors are the reference for shared custom bounds; glass is the reference for a separate render layer.
6. Map it to a sound family in `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` — the `BlockId → MaterialGroup` record is exhaustive, so typecheck fails until the entry exists.
7. Give it a **lighting class** in `lib/world/lighting.ts`: `opacity` (default is fully opaque — air/glass transmit, water/leaves attenuate) and `emission` (default 0; torches emit 14, lava 15). A light source self-illuminates and lights its neighborhood through the shared flood; an opaque block casts shadow. Both are exercised by `lib/world/lighting.test.ts`.
8. The item/recipe integrity tests (`lib/game/config.test.ts`) will fail if a mapping is missing or inconsistent — run `bun test`.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- **World saves move from localStorage to IndexedDB — big builds no longer risk the quota cliff**: a heavily-edited world's save is unbounded JSON, and localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin cap was the likeliest real data loss now that the PWA multiplies long-lived offline worlds ("Save failed" forever once over the line). Saves now live in an IndexedDB store (database `monecraft`) with far larger quotas; existing worlds migrate transparently on first launch (copy-then-delete per world — a mid-migration failure can never lose a blob), and the small profile/world manifests stay in localStorage. The unload save rides `beforeunload`/`visibilitychange`/`pagehide` with an explicitly committed transaction — mobile app-switch now flushes immediately (beforeunload never fired reliably there) instead of waiting for the next 15s autosave. The pause-menu "Saved" toast now means the write durably committed. Browsers without IndexedDB (some private modes) fall back to the old localStorage behavior wholesale; returning players also get a `navigator.storage.persist()` request for eviction protection. Save format itself is unchanged (still v17) — only the container moved; cloud saves and online worlds are untouched.

Dust recipe 1 gold ore + 1 coal → 8 (user-picked); Building category (user re-picked after first choosing a new category); "Circuit Breaker" advancement (17th).

**Why (design invariants):** power state = BlockId parity (ids 58–69, even off/odd on) so toggles ride the save diff — ZERO save/worldgen bumps (v17/worldgen-11 untouched); tickRedstone between tickMobs and tickPrimedTnt is server-only automatically (replica early-return) and replicates via drainEdits → TickMessage.blocks with zero net code; tracked-cell Set seeded from the block diff at boot (craft-only ⇒ diff is a complete census), placement is the only tracking seam, everything else self-heals per 0.1s pass; writes only on change so stable circuits cost nothing.

**How to apply (gotchas found):** (1) `pushBlockCuboid` was X/Z-inset only — extended with minY/maxY (doors pass 0,1). (2) Sources power face neighbors only — diagonals don't; a torch-clock loop needs the wire to physically touch the support pillar's face (first test geometry was wrong). (3) Button countdown needs a 1e-9 epsilon or float drift pops it one pass late. (4) The torch turns off in the SAME pass its support becomes powered (phase-3 reads phase-2's powered set) — clock period is 2 passes. (5) MobState carries `halfHeight` directly — no need for mobHalfHeight(kind) in plate occupancy.

**Verify gate 2026-07-06:** lint (2 pre-existing GameShell warnings) / typecheck / format:check / 1311 unit / build all green; generation.ts + public/ untouched (worldgen hashes unmoved). E2e 30/31 — the multiplayer lagged-break failure is PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN (see below), not redstone.

Passed once solo earlier same day → load-sensitive, now failure-dominant. Needs its own diagnosis session; NOT a redstone or IDB regression (fails identically on pre-branch main).

**Remaining:** user review + push + PR; manual visual pass (atlas tiles on/off contrast, overlay shapes flush, lamp glow at night, no movement snag on wire/plates, NOT gate + clock feel, wire→TNT, powered door, multiplayer lever spot-check per docs/online.md).
